title: Human RNA polymerase III termination favors decomposition over facilitated recycling
task: Characterize RNA polymerase III intrinsic termination mechanisms and pathway branching
key_results: Identified three termination outcomes: decomposing termination (dominant, near-simultaneous RNA-DNA dissociation), recycling termination (2-14%, RNA release with DNA-bound polymerase), and readthrough; longer T-tracts (≥4 thymidines) favor recycling over decomposing pathway
comments: Single-molecule fluorescence provides direct kinetic resolution of mechanistically distinct pathways, though the biological significance of the rare recycling pathway in human RNAP3 versus bacteria suggests species-level regulatory divergence.

model_io.model: Human RNA polymerase III transcription termination

hypotheses.hypothesis: Intrinsic termination proceeds through a single pathway with RNA-DNA simultaneous release
hypotheses.result: Refuted; mechanistic trifurcation identified with two distinct termination modes differing in dissociation kinetics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Facilitated recycling is predominant in human RNAP3 as in bacterial systems
hypotheses.result: Refuted; decomposing termination dominates (86-98%), with recycling accounting for only 2-14%

hypotheses.hypothesis: T-tract length and upstream hairpin structure affect termination efficiency uniformly across pathways
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; longer T-tracts differentially favor recycling, while hairpin effects diminish with distance from T-tracts and affect both pathways similarly

hypotheses.hypothesis: RPC10 subunit mutation broadly impairs termination
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with specificity; selective effects on pathway branching with differential impact on decomposing versus recycling routes

comments: High-resolution spatial proteomics and integrated functional validation provide robust evidence for cardiac aging mechanisms, though FTL1 mechanistic depth lags SERPINA3K characterization.
